a) timed automata patterns are useful in designing real-time systems; b) the patterns can also be used to translate timed process algebra specifications into timed automata; and c) the prototype is a useful tool for system design and analysis using timed automata and process algebra specifications.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of patterns for hierarchical system design using timed models and the development of a tool to automate the design and analysis of such systems.
developing a set of patterns for the hierarchical design of timed automata.

the following: - A formal definition of a set of com-posable patterns for timed automata based on hierarchical constructs of timed process algebras - A prototype tool to support system design with timed automata and to automate the translation of TCOZ specifications into timed automata.

the patterns are useful for the design of complex timed systems.

the patterns allow a systematic design of real-time systems and the translation from TCAZ/TCOZ to timed automaton allows the use of existing tools for verification and analysis.

timed automata patterns can be used to design and verify complex systems in a compositional manner.
